A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KMS Wasserstein research, with matching authors, core definitions and algorithms. All 44 pages of v1 and 34 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison through readable text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: Section V and Appendix L report original timing, solution-quality, testing-power, convergence, kernel-ablation and solution-rank experiments.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix EC.13 report original computational and testing experiments, human-activity detection, image generation, type-I error measurements and rank-reduction results.

M1.justification: The SDR formulation, inexact mirror ascent, OT subroutine and rank-reduction algorithm are retained. v3 adds application-level adaptations using KMS as a generator-training objective and a sliding-window change-detection statistic (Section 5 and EC.12.4), extending rather than replacing the central method.

E1.justification: v3 removes Iris and credit experiments, replaces the blob illustration with noisy concentric circles, and adds Gaussian covariance-shift and image-distribution abundance scenarios. Computational MNIST comparisons change from digits 6/8 to 0/1. CIFAR-10, MSRC-12 human-activity detection and MNIST generation substantially broaden the evaluated populations and tasks.

E2.justification: The two-sample comparison adds Sinkhorn divergence, SW and GSW, replaces optimized MMD-O with Gaussian MMD using median bandwidth, and retains ME and MS. SDR-Naive is renamed SDR-IPM, with participation added in MNIST timing comparisons. The new generation comparison is labelled sliced Wasserstein in Figure 6 and EC.12.4, although Section 5 initially calls it MS.

E3.justification: Computational sweeps extend to n=6400, the reported exact-OT cutoff changes from n<=50 to n<=200, and numerical rank tolerance changes from 1e-20 to 1e-6. Gaussian-mixture testing changes dimension and distribution parameters. New applications introduce detection-delay and FID evaluations and 30-epoch generator training. The activity experiment inconsistently specifies false-alarm rates of 0.01 in the text and 0.05 in Table 1.

E4.justification: v1's convergence-versus-sample-size/dimension study and Gaussian-versus-exponential kernel/bandwidth ablation disappear. v3 adds empirical type-I error checks and replaces four datasets' rank analyses with CIFAR-10 rank measurements and an eigenvalue trajectory demonstrating rank reduction. The nonlinear-projection case study is also replaced and expanded with projected-density plots.

E5.justification: The default reported independent-trial count changes from 10 to 20, although v1 already specifies 20 for testing-power and convergence experiments. v3 introduces testing-power boxplots and explicitly reports means and standard deviations across 10 users in Table 1. This does not establish that every experiment received additional runs.

E6.justification: Computational and testing-power results are substantially replaced under changed settings, while convergence, bandwidth and original rank results are removed. New Table 1 reports mean detection delays of 11.4 for KMS and 12.9 for GSW; Figure 6 reports FID 0.0335 for KMS versus 0.0537 for the baseline labelled SW. Table EC.2 adds type-I error estimates ranging from 0.042 to 0.062. These are new outcomes, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v3 adds a metric-property theorem, positive-definiteness conditions for G in EC.4, and Theorem 8's multiplicative SDR value bound with a new proof in EC.9. Theorem 2 extends v1's null-only two-sample statement to arbitrary population pairs. Its one-sample guarantee already existed in v1 Proposition 20; the computational lemmas are likewise relocated rather than newly established.

C1.justification: The central claims of dimension-free concentration, NP-hardness, efficient SDR computation and low-rank solutions remain. The contribution list and conclusion broaden the empirical applicability claims to human-activity detection and generative modeling, replacing the earlier emphasis on uncertainty quantification. Both abstracts already claim a relaxation-gap guarantee.

C2.justification: v3 removes the lack of objective-value guarantees from the limitations and describes its new approximation ratio as conservative. Interpretation shifts from frequent rank-one/exact SDR solutions in v1 to demonstrating the need for rank reduction on CIFAR-10. It adds an explanation of MS's advantage for Gaussian covariance shifts, while removing the convergence and kernel-bandwidth interpretations accompanying the deleted analyses.

D1.justification: EC.12 expands the experimental recipes with a 50/50 testing split, 500 permutation examples, explicit distribution-abundance mixtures, Kinect preprocessing, and a four-layer leaky-ReLU generator trained for 30 epochs. These include newly documented procedures rather than established changes to previously unspecified settings. MS implementation access changes from the KPW repository to POT; original Iris/credit preprocessing details and the MMD-O implementation pointer disappear.

R1.justification: The existing MS/KMS research positioning largely remains. A focused new appendix compares OT families by time and sample complexity, supported by additional references on Sinkhorn sample complexity, spiked transport, quadratic-relaxation bounds and positive-definite kernels. Dataset and application references also change; preprint-to-publication updates do not constitute new related works.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites and reorganizes the introduction's contribution discussion, streamlines the computational narrative, and moves v1 Lemmas 13–14 into EC.8. The numerical-study narrative and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Appendices are reorganized into EC sections, and the separate broader-societal-impact section is removed.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a denser journal layout and substantially redesigns the displays: runtime curves become grouped bars, testing-power curves become multipanel boxplots, and new projection, rank-reduction, activity and generation figures appear. It adds comparison and error tables while removing the original rank-bound plot, ablation plots and four rank tables. The NP-hardness diagram is retained in the supplement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds broader validation, useful implementation guidance and an explicit SDR value-gap argument addressing a limitation stated in v1. However, it removes convergence and kernel-sensitivity evidence and introduces material inconsistencies: Table EC.1 gives KMS_p an n^-1/2 rate despite Theorem 2's n^-1/(2p) rate; activity false-alarm rates conflict; and EC.3 retains the null-case proof without the population-distance term needed for the generalized theorem. These benefits and shortcomings prevent a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
